title: Add benchmark-lab representative workload runners and reporting pipeline v3
author: Ava Chen
description: This PR upgrades the benchmark-lab to v3 of the representative workload runners and adds a reporting pipeline that centralizes perf baselines and visualizations. Motivation: the v2 runners were brittle under variable seq-len distributions and produced noisy baselines; the new runners are workload-driven (chat completion, long-form generation, embedding batch loads, and streaming scenarios) and include deterministic replay of recorded request traces. The reporting pipeline pushes normalized metrics (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, memory/gpu utilization, kernel breakdown) and artifacts (flamegraphs, pprof traces, sample traces) to the reporting service and builds a per-run comparison page. Checklist: - [x] Add deterministic workload runner harness for representative workloads - [x] Add sample traces and trace serializer for replay - [x] Integrate lightweight BPF sampling + pprof export for profiling baselines - [x] Add pipeline job to upload artifacts to the reporting S3 bucket and trigger comparison job - [x] Add dashboard templates (Grafana/LookerLite) and example queries - [x] CI job to run a small smoke perf suite on PRs and upload results to a temporary bucket - [x] Docs: benchmark-lab/README and runbook for interpreting regressions Notes: The reporting pipeline supports run tags and model/version metadata so we can attribute regressions to model changes or infra. This PR does not change production serving codepaths; it only affects benchmark tooling and CI orchestration. Related Linear: ENG-8123 (representative workload runners), ENG-8450 (reporting pipeline UX).

release_notes: Added benchmark-lab v3: deterministic representative workload runners, BPF/pprof profiling hooks, and a reporting pipeline that centralizes perf baselines and artifacts. Includes new CI perf-smoke job and dashboard templates.
motivation_and_context: Teams running long-running generative workloads need reproducible performance baselines and a simple way to detect regressions. This change standardizes how we run representative workloads, collect profiles, and present diffs so infra and model teams can iterate faster.
notes_for_release_engineering: No production code changed. Release teams should ensure the reporting S3 bucket has lifecycle policy and credentials for CI jobs. Add the optional bpf_sampler binary to the benchmark-lab images for Linux runners where kernel supports eBPF.
